messages:
Maya: ok quick draft attached — goal: a short, low-touch bench email that drives dev signups and a light demo. This is NOT the deep whitepaper, it's a 3-chart tease + one clear CTA.

Maya: thinking structure: 1) headline that sells predictable inference, 2) 3 micro-charts (latency vs cost, batch efficiency, p99 tail), 3) one short customer quote, 4) CTA -> try hosted sandbox or schedule a quick demo.

Maya: subject line options: `Try Redwood Inference — predictable latency, lower token cost` or `See how inference costs fall when latency stays predictable`. Thoughts?

Alex: prefer tighter subject. how about `Predictable latency. Lower inference costs. Try it.` short & punchy.

Sam: +1 to short. For charts: skip jargon. Chart labels should read plain English: e.g., "Average latency (ms)" on y axis, "Cost per 1k tokens (USD)" on x axis for scatter.

Sam: also propose a tiny annotation on chart 1: "Auto batching reduces cost by up to 3x at 99th percentile for typical prompt mixes" (we can back that with benchmark link).

Priya: For audience segmentation: we should A/B the CTA for two segments — SMB devs (self-serve sandbox) vs Platform teams (book demo). Email should route clickers to different landing forms so SDRs get enterprise signals.

Priya: Routing plan: clicks with company email -> ask a single extra Q -> flag in HubSpot. personal emails -> sandbox + inline quickstart.

Rachel: copy nits: lead with problem users feel: "Your inference bill spikes unpredictably during peak user queries" then offer the 3-chart postcard to show determinism. Keep hero copy under 40 chars.

Maya: good call. I'll make hero: `Stop guessing inference costs` subhead: `Real numbers for latency and dollars — pick the tradeoff that fits you.`

Alex: for the three charts, suggested captions: 1) "Deterministic latency vs token spend" 2) "Batching & KV cache: unit cost impact" 3) "Tail latency at scale" — each with one-sentence takeaway.

Sam: For visuals, can we do a tiny interactive or GIF for the batching effect? If not, an annotated PNG with a slider image works for email.

Maya: interactive is heavier; let's ship PNG + a short GIF for the batching effect. Dev hint below the fold: link to small JS sandbox and `curl` example.

Priya: CTA copy options: `Try sandbox — 5 minutes to run your model` vs `See enterprise options` (two buttons). We'll track via UTM and split by domain.

Rachel: A/B test subject lines and hero CTAs. Group A: urgency phrasing. Group B: economics phrasing. Run for 1 week, 5k recipients first pass.

Maya: timeline: draft email by EOD Wed, design + charts Thu, internal review Fri morning, send next Tue. Is that realistic?

Alex: timeline ok but need bench numbers confirmed — will ping eng to verify the numbers and provide CSV charts by Wed noon.

Sam: quick ask to eng: include both hosted vs dedicated numbers and a quantized 4-bit profile. We can annotate that quantization impacts accuracy — link to eval.

Maya: I'll add a short blurb: "Accuracy preserved in most user flows; see our evals" with a link. Keep claims conservative.

marketing-bot: Scheduled: A/B test created (campaign id: camp_6321). Draft saved to Google Drive: https://drive.redwood/test-mini-bench.

Priya: tagging for SDRs — can someone add a note to the campaign with routing rules and the HubSpot form id? I'll do the mapping but need the form id.

Alex: I'll add the required metadata once eng numbers land.

Rachel: small creative ask: include a micro testimonial from Platform Beta customer (one line) — e.g., "Cut p99 latency variability in half" — need legal sign-off.

Maya: I'll loop in legal after draft.

Sam: last thing — add a short inline code snippet for devs showing how to run a 50-token test and measure latency: ```bash
curl -X POST \"https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate\" -H 'Authorization: Bearer <KEY>' -d '{"model":"open-instruct-lite","prompt":"Hello","max_tokens":50}'
```

Maya: perfect. I'll assemble and upload. Thanks all — please jump on comments in the Drive doc. :rocket:
